quizName:
Hardest Questions in Nebraska
									  					
									  														  					Most difficult questions from your region.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: These parking spaces are for people with disabled parking permits.
Traffic in this lane must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.
These lanes are for buses and cars with 2 or more people.

questions.correctAnswerText: These parking spaces are for people with disabled parking permits.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces reserved for people with disabled parking permits.

questions.question: Children up to age 18 cannot ride in cargo areas.
questions.explanation: Children up to age 18 cannot ride in the cargo area of a vehicle. They must wear a safety belt or sit in a child safety seat while the vehicle is moving.

questions.question: When stopped by police for a traffic violation or equipment check, you must show:
questions.explanation: You must have your license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance when driving. All three documents must be shown if stopped by police.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A red circle with a red line through it means the action is not allowed. This sign means you cannot turn right.

questions.question: When driving in a work zone, you should:

options.text: Pay attention, follow all signs, drive at a safe speed, and be ready to stop.
Drive faster so you don't slow down traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pay attention, follow all signs, drive at a safe speed, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: In a work zone, stay alert and obey posted signs. Drive at a steady, safe speed. Leave space for workers and equipment. Be ready to stop at any time.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means left turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Barricades, panels, drums, and cones are used to guide drivers safely through work zones.
questions.explanation: Barricades, panels, drums, and cones guide drivers safely through work zones. Be careful when passing through.

questions.question: Before turning right on a red light, you should:

options.text: Slow down and go if the way is clear.
Stop completely, look both ways, and let pedestrians and other traffic go first.
Keep your speed because you have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, look both ways, and let pedestrians and other traffic go first.
questions.explanation: You may turn right at a red light unless a sign says you cannot. Always stop first, look both ways, and yield to pedestrians and other traffic.

questions.question: If you see an aggressive driver, you should:
questions.explanation: If you see an aggressive driver, get out of their way. Do not compete with other drivers. This keeps you safe.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells drivers that pedestrians may be crossing. Be alert and ready to stop.

questions.question: When you encounter an aggressive driver, what should you do?

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Make sure they know you disapprove of their driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and create distance between you and the other driver. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact or make rude gestures.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn at this location.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Talking or texting on a cell phone.
Changing a radio station or CD.

questions.explanation: Drivers must make many decisions while driving. Any extra task can take your attention away from driving and create danger.

questions.question: If you become tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Stop to rest or change drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to rest or change drivers.
questions.explanation: Stop to rest or find another driver. Being tired slows your reactions and makes driving unsafe.

questions.question: If you have had an argument and feel angry, what should you do before driving?

options.text: Play the radio loudly so you won't think about the argument.
Take a few minutes to calm down.
Drive on the interstate to let off steam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down.
questions.explanation: Your emotions affect how well you drive. If you are angry, scared, worried, or upset, take time to calm down before driving. You need to focus on the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you that a traffic signal is coming. Be ready to stop for a red light or slow down for a yellow light.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with sirens and flashing lights approaches, you should pull to the right and wait for it to pass.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights and/or sirens approaches, immediately move to the right side of the road and let it pass.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Stop at the nearest rest area to rest, nap, stretch, or switch drivers. Caffeine pills are not a safe replacement for sleep.

questions.question: When should you slow down while driving?

options.text: When the road is wet or slippery.

questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, near intersections, near railroad crossings, on hills, in curves, near pedestrians, and when roads are wet or slippery.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you a steep hill is coming. Slow down to protect your brakes and avoid a crash.

questions.question: Before turning, you should:
questions.explanation: Always turn on your signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn. This warns other drivers.

questions.question: Which is true about airbags in a vehicle?

options.text: Drivers with airbags do not need to wear safety belts.
Airbags work best when used with safety belts.
Children age 12 and under can sit safely in the front seat with airbags.

questions.correctAnswerText: Airbags work best when used with safety belts.
questions.explanation: Airbags and safety belts work together to protect you. Airbags are not a replacement for safety belts. Children age 12 and under should sit in the rear seat because airbags can injure them.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reserved parking for persons with disabilities.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces reserved for people with disabilities. Only vehicles with disability license plates or placards can park here.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign tells you which direction you must drive on a one-way street.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign is placed at the start of one-way streets. It means you cannot drive in your current direction.
